Falco's default shell detection rule triggers on proc.name in (sh, bash, zsh, dash). What other programs can execute code and read files?

python3 -c "print(open('/secret/flag').read())" — Python can read files directly without spawning a named shell. kubectl exec -n dojo-sec-evasion red-team-pod -- python3 -c "print(open('/secret/flag').read())"

Three other approaches that bypass the name-based rule: awk's getline, find -exec cat, or any language interpreter (perl, ruby, node). The defense is to use eBPF syscall-level detection instead of proc.name matching.
